angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 392,375 km at 184.58 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4178 +/- 0.0115 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 184.58 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.564 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Morello et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7009 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract): 392,375 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.583 +/- 0.014 solar masses from Morello et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7009 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4080 +/- 25 K from Morello et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7009 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Morello et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7009 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7009.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.701, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7009 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.11 dex, from Morello et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-7009 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.88845, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
